headline: Commodities Briefing: Metals Slip on Tech Optimism as European Gas Surges
paragraphs: Natural gas spiked 11.24 percent today, extending a massive monthly gain of 34.17 percent, driven by a forecast cold snap in Europe that fed supply shortage fears and pushed reserves below 73 percent. This weather-driven energy squeeze is already impacting wholesale electricity prices, which have more than doubled over the past year.

Precious and industrial metals faced heavy downward pressure over the week despite brief intraday bounces. Silver dropped 2.59 percent today and over 11 percent for the week, while platinum fell 3.02 percent and copper slid 2.41 percent. Markets are heavily fixated on upcoming US inflation and PCE data to gauge the Federal Reserve rate path, with a strong US dollar capping rebounds.

Copper did roar back during intraday trading alongside gold and platinum, a move fueled by bargain buying and a revival of the AI trade following Nvidia news involving Jensen Huang. However, broader monthly trends remain deep in the red, with silver down over 21 percent and platinum shedding 17 percent over the last month.

WTI crude edged down 0.57 percent today and over 7 percent for the week, pressured by increased Middle Eastern supplies and a growing global supply surplus amid Gulf attacks, leaving Irish consumers wondering why pump prices are not dropping faster. The euro traded at 1.0913 against the US dollar.
